**Answer: 34 (best construction found; not proven optimal)**

**Lower bound.** For positive integers $a_1<\dots<a_{10}$, the chain $a_1a_1<a_1a_2<\dots<a_1a_{10}<a_2a_{10}<\dots<a_{10}a_{10}$ gives $|AA|\ge 2n-1=19$, and similarly $|A+A|\ge 19$. This only gives $M\ge 19$.

**Construction.** Take $A=\{2^i3^j : (i,j)\in S\}$ with $S=\{(i,j): i,j\ge 0,\ i+j\le 3\}$, which has 10 points. The elements are
$$A=\{1,2,3,4,6,8,9,12,18,27\}.$$

- **Products:** $(i,j)+(k,l)$ ranges over all lattice points with nonnegative coordinates and coordinate sum $\le 6$. There are $\binom{8}{2}=28$ such points, so $|AA|=28$.
- **Sums:** Enumerating all $\binom{10}{2}+10=55$ pairwise sums and removing duplicates gives $|A+A|=34$. The distinct values are $2,\dots,22$ (21 values) together with $24,26,27,28,29,30,31,33,35,36,39,45,54$ (13 values).

So $\max(|A+A|,|AA|)=\max(34,28)=34$, giving $M\le 34$.

**Caveats.** I did not run an exhaustive search. I tried a few other shapes (a $5\times2$ grid of exponents gave $|A+A|=40$; a $3\times3$ grid plus one extra point gave $\max=36$), and the triangle was the best of these. A different set could do better, so 34 is an upper bound on $M$ rather than a verified minimum.

ANSWER: 34
